projects.name: Improved access to bread through bread subsidy project
projects.description: Bread is a central component of the Syrian diet, accounting for around one third of daily caloric intake, yet worsening food insecurity affecting over 9 million people and shortfalls in national wheat production have made affordable bread increasingly difficult to access, with recent subsidy reductions driving sharp price increases and deepening hardship among vulnerable families. In response, WFP, in partnership with the Government of Syria through the Ministry of Economy and Industry, launched the Subsidized Bread Programme in 2025 to stabilize access, reduce household economic pressure, and support national food security by supplying WFP provided wheat flour to selected bakeries, enabling 2 million people in the most food insecure areas to purchase fortified bread at a fixed subsidized price that covers only operational costs while safeguarding access to a daily staple.

projects.name: Palestine refugees are able to meet their essential needs and cope with sudden crises in dignity MPCA
projects.description:
Vulnerable Palestine refugees are provided with multi- purpose cash assistance:
UNRWA aims to maintain MPCA as a core pillar of its 2026 humanitarian response in Syria. The Agency will extend MPCA support to 7,000 Palestinian refugee households (24,500 individuals), primarily those residing in Yarmouk, Ein el-Tal, and Dera’a camps, identified as most vulnerable through needs-based targeting.

- Shock-affected Palestine refugees are provided with emergency multi-purpose cash assistance (EMPCA):
To support households affected by new humanitarian shocks including armed conflict, climate-related events and situations of unrest, the Agency will provide EMPCA to 3,000 affected households (10,500 individuals). Each family will receive US$ 150 per month for three months to stabilize household economies following a crisis and help them meet essential needs.
- Palestine refugee returnee households are provided with a reintegration grant:
In 2026, UNRWA will also support dignified, sustainable and voluntary return through targeted support for Palestine refugees. A total of 6,500 cross-border returnee and internally displaced households (22,750 individuals), moving to their areas of origin or return will receive a one-off payment of US$ 600, intended to cover basic return and reintegration needs for an initial four-month period, equivalent to four months of the EMPCA transfer (US$ 150), in line with the Cash Working Group (CWG) guidance and harmonized with similar UNHCR support for Syrian returnees.

projects.name: UNRWA students are  provided with quality,  inclusive and equitable  education
projects.description:
UNRWA will continue to deliver quality, inclusive and equitable elementary and preparatory education to approximately 52,000 Palestine refugee students enrolled across 100 schools in Syria. To address capacity constraints resulting from conflict damage and population movements, particularly in Yarmouk camp, the Agency will operate around 58 double-shift schools, utilizing both UNRWA facilities and premises provided by the Ministry of Education.
To support learning continuity, around 5,500 students will benefit from catch-up classes, while all students will receive back-to-school kits and participate in at least one recreational or extra-curricular activity during the academic year. In addition, 3,000 students will participate in summer recreational programmes.
UNRWA will also rehabilitate or reconstruct five conflict-damaged schools across its areas of operation in 2026, including in Yarmouk, Khan El-Shieh, Hussienieh, and Dera’a. Furthermore, the Agency will undertake the repair and maintenance of all 36 school premises to ensure safe and functional learning environments.
TVET: UNRWA’s TVET programme will offer long and short-term courses for 1,930 trainees in its vocational training centres (VTCs)
